title: Harmonic Nanoparticles for Regenerative Research
protocol: Prepare the cell propagation medium containing Knockout DMEM supplemented with specified additives.
Thaw human ESC in 8 ml of prepared PM medium.
Centrifuge at 115 x g for 5 min to discard freezing medium.
Add 1 ml of PM medium with 10 mM Rock inhibitor and incubate for 24 hours.
Supplement the PM medium with basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) at a concentration between 4-10 ng/ml.
Plate hESC on irradiated human foreskin feeder cells previously plated at 2 x 10^4 cells/cm².
Change medium daily and remove differentiating colonies by aspiration when necessary.
Once a week, passage colonies enzymatically: Remove the medium and wash with PBS.
Incubate colonies with collagenase IV for 10 minutes at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Collect colony fragments in new PM and centrifuge at 115 x g for 3 min.
Alternatively, pass colonies mechanically by scraping using a StemPro EZPassage roller scraper tool.
Collect colony fragments and centrifuge them for 3 min at 115 x g to remove the supernatant.
Plate fragments on γHFF or process them for differentiation into embryoid bodies (EBs).

Prepare the differentiation medium (DM) using Knockout DMEM supplemented with 2% Hyclone serum, 1.0% MEM Non-Essential Amino Acids, 1.0% L-glutamine 200 mM, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, and 3.5 µl β-mercaptoethanol.
Remove medium and wash colonies with 2 ml PBS.
Incubate colony fragments with 0.5 ml per well of warm collagenase IV at 1 mg/ml for 10 min at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Collect colony fragments in 2 ml new DM and centrifuge them at 115 x g for 3 min.
Culture the collected fragments in suspension in ultra-low attachment 6-well plates (2 ml per well) for 4 days.
Collect newly formed EBs and plate them on 0.1% gelatin-coated 24-well plates (about 3 EBs/well).
Remove PBS and dissociate colonies into single cells using accutase (0.5 ml/well).
Centrifuge the cells and resuspend them in DM at a concentration of 1.2 x 10^6/ml.
Add 2 ml per Aggrewell chamber for 1 day.
Collect newly formed EBs and plate them on 0.1% gelatin-coated 24-well plates (about 3 EBs/well).
Change the differentiation medium every 2-3 days until the appearance of beating clusters of cardiomyocytes (15-30 days).
Identify clusters of beating cardiomyocytes after 2-4 weeks of culture.
Manually dissect identified clusters using an elongated sharply cut Pasteur pipette.
Deposit 4 PTFE filters per insert on a 6-well plate.
Add 1 ml of DM medium to each well containing the PTFE filters.
Place one dissected beating cluster on each PTFE filter, with a maximum of 4 clusters per well.
Change the DM medium every 2-3 days.
Remove the PTFE filter containing the beating cluster and place it on a 3.5 cm glass bottom dish (170 µm thick).
Add 1 ml of HNP at a concentration of 50 µg/ml to the dissected cluster for 30 min.
Transfer either whole differentiating early hEBs or cardiac beating clusters to PTFE filters over a 170 µm thick glass-bottom dish compatible with high numerical aperture objectives.
Alternatively, coat the glass-bottom dish pre-coated with 0.1% gelatin and apply direct coating of beating clusters to it.
Transfer samples to an all-in-one microscope equipped with an incubating chamber for stable temperature, humidity, and CO2 control.
Perform initial inspection via wide-field imaging under white light illumination.
Identify structures of interest within differentiated EBs or active beating clusters for further investigations.
Set a shorter laser excitation wavelength of 720 nm.
Use a narrow band-pass spectral filter centered at 360 ± 10 nm to detect SH.
Use another narrow band-pass spectral filter to detect autofluorescence.
Perform a fast, low resolution three-dimensional scan to rebuild the overall morphology of the cardiac cluster.
Select an image plane within the cluster volume with several visible HNPs.
Change the excitation wavelength freely to best match the sample's optical properties or to avoid photobleaching and photo damage.
Adjust the excitation wavelength to 790 nm for imaging deeper into tissues.
Replace the second harmonic filter accordingly at 395 nm.
Optimize the settings of the laser pulse pre-compressor by maximizing the second harmonic signal of HNPs on the sample.
Set the microscope optical scanner in resonant mode for high speed acquisition of two-dimensional images.
Choose scan averaging of 4 for a compromise between image contrast and acquisition speed.
Set the pixel dwell time to 0.1 µsec.
Acquire images at an image rate of 3.75 frames per second (fps).
Adjust laser power according to focal spot size and scanning speed.
Set typical laser power to 50 mW at the entrance of the objective.
Select a single HNP deposited on a bare substrate for calibration.
Maximize SH intensity by adjusting focus to the optimal axial position.
Vary the axial position of the microscope stage systematically.
Obtain the calibration curve relating SH intensity to HNP offset from focal plane.
Automate the procedure to select HNPs present in all video frames.
Determine periodic movements of selected HNPs across video frames.
Assess the quantification of out-of-plane displacements associated with non-continuously traceable HNPs moving along the optical axis.
Convert intensity modulations throughout different frames into axial displacement using the calibration curve established at Step 5.1.
Note that this procedure gives access to axial movements but cannot determine the absolute direction (upwards or downwards).
